strings.name: Yuzuru Hanyu
strings.summary: Yuzuru Hanyu won men’s Olympic gold in 2014 and 2018 and two world titles, reaching international audiences through technical innovation, musical expression and complete programmes. In 2022 he left competition for professional performance, creating solo shows and ICE STORY projects. REALIVE’s Miyagi performances were completed in April 2026; the November Saga encore remained future at this dossier’s cutoff.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 16, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: An Olympic champion and technical innovator who expanded figure skating’s international audiences and performance influence.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: Consecutive Olympic titles
strings.highlights.h1.text: Gold in Sochi in 2014 and PyeongChang in 2018 made him the first men’s repeat champion in decades.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Started at four, attended Tohoku High School and studied Human Information Science through Waseda’s distance programme, graduating in 2020.
strings.highlights.h2.title: From technique to solo creation
strings.highlights.h2.text: Landed the first quadruple loop in international competition and later integrated skating, narrative, music and stage production.
strings.timeline.t1.title: REALIVE in Miyagi
strings.timeline.t1.text: Completed two performances on April 11–12; the announced Saga encore on November 28–29 had not occurred by November 16.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Echoes of Life began
strings.timeline.t2.text: Launched another ICE STORY tour combining solo skating, original narrative and audiovisual design, continuing into 2025.
strings.timeline.t3.title: GIFT at Tokyo Dome
strings.timeline.t3.text: Staged a solo ice show at Tokyo Dome, extending the venue scale and narrative form of individual skating performance.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Professional transition
strings.timeline.t4.text: Announced his departure from competitive events for professional skating, continuing training and creative performance.
strings.timeline.t5.title: PyeongChang title defense
strings.timeline.t5.text: Won a second Olympic men’s gold after overcoming injuries during the season.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Second world championship
strings.timeline.t6.text: Won in Helsinki after a free-skate comeback, adding to his first world title from 2014.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Sochi Olympic gold
strings.timeline.t7.text: Became the first Asian Olympic men’s singles champion and won his first senior world title that year.
strings.timeline.t8.title: World Junior champion
strings.timeline.t8.text: Won the junior men’s title, preparing for senior competition and further international training.
